newsitem.title: ITALY: Peron "daughter" says exhumation to be set in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Peron "daughter" says exhumation to be set in Feb.

text.p: An Argentine woman who wants to prove she is the illegitimate daughter of late president Juan Peron, said in an interview published on Sunday that a court would set a date in early February for the exhumation of his body.
"Very soon we'll know the whole truth," Martha Holgado, 62, told Italy's La Repubblica in an interview from Buenos Aires.
"(The judge) has decided that in the first week of February, the day and time of the exhumation will finally be fixed."
Holgado returned to Buenos Aires from her home in Madrid last September after winning an appeal to open the tomb of the man who ruled Argentina from 1946-55 and 1973-74.
DNA tests will be carried out on the embalmed body to check whether Holgado's blood matches genetic material from Peron.

Holgado, who bears a striking resemblance to the late populist leader, says Peron and her mother were lovers in 1932 but she did not learn she was his daughter until she was 19 and never told anyone because of a pact of secrecy with her mother.
"They said my father was impotent or sterile," Holgado said. "Clearly he wasn't because the proof is here, in my blood."
Holgado has accused Peron's third wife Maria Estela Martinez, known as Isabel, of deliberately obstructing her legal fight.
Isabel, who became president when Peron died in office in 1974 but was toppled by a military coup in 1976, does not want his tomb in the capital's La Chacarita cemetery opened.
